case.title: Will the seasonally adjusted CPI-U all items index increase by 0.1% or more in July 2026, as first published by the BLS?
case.resolution_rule: YES if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Price Index news release for July 2026 reports a one-month percent change in the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), all items, of 0.1 percent or more, as first published in that release and rounded to one decimal place as BLS prints it. NO if the reported one-month change is less than 0.1 percent. Later revisions are ignored. The threshold is the top bucket of the Polymarket market for this print (0.1% or more), which is the same event as the Kalshi market 'Above 0.0%' (a one-decimal change strictly greater than 0.0%). The buckets of one print are mutually exclusive outcomes of one figure; they are scored as this single yes/no question, not as separate events.

evidence.title: BLS news release: Consumer Price Index - June 2026 (verbatim excerpt: opening summary paragraphs)
evidence.content:
CONSUMER PRICE INDEX - JUNE 2026

The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) decreased 0.4 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in June after rising 0.5 percent in May, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. This decline in the all items index was the largest 1-month decrease since April 2020 when it fell 0.8 percent. Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 3.5 percent before seasonal adjustment.

The index for energy fell 5.7 percent in June after rising 3.9 percent in May, 3.8 percent in April, and 10.9 percent in March. The energy index was the largest contributor to the monthly all items decrease, more than offsetting increases in other indexes including those for shelter and food. The index for food increased 0.2 percent over the month, as did the index for food at home and the index for food away from home.

The index for all items less food and energy was unchanged in June. Indexes that decreased over the month include motor vehicle insurance, communication, apparel, medical care, and used cars and trucks. Conversely, the indexes for recreation, household furnishings and operations, and personal care were among the major indexes that increased in June.

The all items index rose 3.5 percent for the 12 months ending June after rising 4.2 percent for the 12 months ending May. The all items less food and energy index rose 2.6 percent over the year, following a 2.9-percent increase over the 12 months ending May. The energy index increased 15.7 percent for the 12 months ending June. The food index increased 3.0 percent over the last year.

evidence.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement (July 29, 2026; full statement text)
evidence.content:
The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 9 – 3 vote:

The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.

Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East. Productivity growth and capital investment are strong. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.

Inflation remains elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy. The Committee will deliver price stability.

Voting against the monetary policy action were Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie K. Logan, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

evidence.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, June 16-17, 2026 (verbatim excerpt: paragraphs containing 'outlook for monetary policy')
evidence.content: With regard to the outlook for monetary policy, amid high assessed uncertainty, various participants discussed a range of scenarios for the evolution of the economy and for future monetary policy actions. Most participants remarked on scenarios in which inflationary pressures would dissipate and inflation would soon begin to return to 2 percent. In such scenarios, almost all of these participants noted that it would likely be appropriate to maintain or eventually lower the target range for the federal funds rate. Most participants, however, also pointed to scenarios in which, in the context of stable labor market conditions, inflation would remain elevated due to strong AI-related demand, the conflict in the Middle East, or the effects of tariffs. In such scenarios, almost all of these participants indicated that some policy firming would likely be warranted to return inflation to 2 percent. Regarding participants' individual assessments of appropriate monetary policy under what each participant judged to be the most likely scenario for the economy, many participants indicated that the appropriate level of the federal funds rate would be within or slightly below the current target range at the end of this year. Many other participants, however, assessed that the appropriate level of the federal funds rate would be above the current target range at the end of this year. Participants noted that their future policy actions would depend on incoming information.

curation_notes.as_of_rule: 00:00:00 UTC, 7 calendar days before the BLS release date (2026-08-12, 8:30 a.m. ET)
curation_notes.contamination: Default replay model llama3.1:8b: knowledge cutoff December 2023 (Meta model card). This 2026 event is after that cutoff, so contamination_flag = unlikely (never 'none'). Check any other model's card first. The curator (Claude, training data to about mid-2026) may itself know the answer; the mechanical rule is what stops that from steering case or evidence choice.

evidence_classification.cpi-2026-jul.cpi: Official BLS statistical release, verbatim excerpt. documentary_fact: measured price changes as first published for an earlier month (not the print being forecast; later revisions are not reflected).
evidence_classification.cpi-2026-jul.statement: Official FOMC policy statement. documentary_fact: the policy action and vote it records; analyst_interpretation: the Committee's own description of the economy, including inflation, and its forward guidance (official guidance, not a numeric forecast).
evidence_classification.cpi-2026-jul.minutes: Official minutes, verbatim excerpt. analyst_interpretation: summarized views of FOMC participants on the outlook for policy, as written by the FOMC Secretariat (not individual quotes, not a numeric forecast).
evidence_classification.cpi-2026-jul.nowcast: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland model output, verbatim values from the archived data file. forecast: a statistical model's daily estimate of this month's CPI change, made before the release. It is not the print and carries model error.

curation_notes.excerpt_method: Verbatim. Same extraction code as #54/#67. Fed pages fetched live on observed_at; HTML tags removed, entities decoded, runs of whitespace collapsed, paragraphs joined with a blank line; each paragraph was also found verbatim (whitespace-normalized) in the archive_url capture, dated before as_of. BLS pages refuse automated requests (HTTP 403), so BLS text is taken from the archive_url capture (before as_of) of the permanent BLS archive URL; each excerpt paragraph was also found in a second pre-as_of capture of the BLS current-release page. Cleveland Fed nowcast: values copied as strings from the chart for this month in the latest pre-as_of capture of nowcast_month.json (no rounding); that capture's 'Actual CPI Inflation' values for this month were empty. The live file shows current data only, so this item is archive-only.
curation_notes.release_times: BLS: 'embargoed until 8:30 a.m. (ET)' (13:30 UTC standard time, 12:30 UTC daylight time). FOMC statements and minutes: 'For release at 2:00 p.m. EST/EDT' as printed (19:00 / 18:00 UTC). Cleveland Fed nowcast: the file states an update stamp without a time zone, so published_at = available_at = the archive capture time, a verifiable upper bound.
curation_notes.human_check: Each evidence item is listed in docs/curation/VERIFY_82.md for the finance owner's confirmation (#82). Not admitted until ticked there.

market.quotes_included: every saved quote with as_of - 24h <= ts <= as_of (the gate's selection window); the full series stays in data/raw
market.venue_rule_differences: Polymarket YES = one-month change of the seasonally adjusted CPI-U of 0.1% or more (one decimal). Kalshi YES = 'Above 0.0%'; the KXCPI contract terms define the Underlying as the one-month, one-decimal change in the seasonally adjusted CPI-U published by BLS, first published (revisions after expiration ignored), payout strictly greater than the level. On one-decimal values these are the same event. They differ only if BLS does not publish on schedule (Kalshi extends expiry; Polymarket's later markets wait until the next scheduled CPI release, then use the most recent previous month); rule 5 requires the release on the venues' date. Market rule text read on 2026-11-14 through the repo adapters (not stored); the KXCPI contract terms PDF read on the same day is the current version and may differ from the one in force then.
